facts.text: East Liverpool earned the nickname “Ceramic City” because its pottery industry once dominated the U.S. market.
The downtown historic district spans 22 acres and showcases Italianate and Second Empire buildings that once housed the city’s thriving commerce.
In 1893, Moorish‑ and Persian‑influenced pottery from East Liverpool won awards at the Chicago World’s Columbian Exposition.
The city’s Carnegie library, opened in 1902, was the first of Ohio’s Carnegie libraries and remains a landmark of early 20th‑century architecture.
East Liverpool sits on the Ohio River where the borders of Ohio, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia meet, about 30 miles from Pittsburgh.
The Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail, commemorating the 1804–06 expedition, passes through East Liverpool, linking the town to a national legacy.
